answers.answer: In 3 players, the tied leaders receive no coin, and the uniquely last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Census: a tied lead gives no coin; unique last pays 1; in a 2-player game last never pays.

answers.answer: No. You may draw any number up to six, limited by free Market spaces, so you cannot draw more than the two free spaces permit. Followers left on the Market remain between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Followers: draw any number up to allowance, limited by free Market spaces; unused Market Followers remain and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds, but it activates only when all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall needs only one of its two spaces). You may not execute it before it is full. A fully activated action may be saved for a later round. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology stays in place.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Planning and Actions: fill gradually; action activates only when all required spaces are occupied; activation can be saved; ordinary action Followers return to bag.

answers.answer: Starting with the Start Player, players go clockwise repeatedly, each taking one activated action or passing. You choose the order of your actions. Once you pass, you cannot act again that Action Phase, even with unused activations; unused activations retain their Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Actions: one activated action or passing; passing ends participation; unused activations keep their Followers.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances your Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted at that track space.
answers.evidence: Actions table: Farm House — Boatman + Craftsman; put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.

answers.answer: Village recruits one of a Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader into your bag and advances that profession's track one space. Boatman gives the depicted coins (at the last space, the first player there gets a Citizen instead of coins); Craftsman gives a Technology tile (usable only after you pass); Trader gives a Place Tile (first advance category I only; later advances category I or II).
answers.evidence: Village recruitment: put chosen neutral Follower in bag and advance its profession's track; listed Boatman, Craftsman, and Trader rewards.

answers.answer: No. A Craftsman-acquired Technology is usable only after you pass, so it cannot help another action that round after passing. Your first placed Technology must replace a Farmer. Technology cannot be moved after placement; later ones may replace any profession except Monk; at most one Technology per Place, and none at a Place requiring only one Follower. A Craftsman-acquired tile is used only after passing.
answers.evidence: Technology placement limits; Village recruitment: Craftsman tile is used only after you pass.

answers.answer: No. The first Traders Track advance permits category I only. Every later advance permits category I or II. Players may inspect the Place Tile stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Setup: players may inspect stacks at any time. Village recruitment: first Traders Track advance permits category I only; every later advance allows I or II.

answers.answer: University puts a Scholar in your bag, advances the Scholars Track one space, and gives its depicted Development Points. Castle puts a Knight in your bag and advances the Knights Track; the fourth Knight leaves the draw allowance at 7, and the first player to reach that space takes its Citizen. Monastery puts a Monk in your bag with no extra track reward. The summary says the fourth Knight leaves the allowance at 7; it does not state what the draw allowance is immediately before the fourth-Knight step. Once a character track is on its last space, you cannot take that corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: Actions table: University, Castle, Monastery; Castle rewards; Character-track limits.

answers.answer: Yes. On ordinary actions a Monk can replace any other profession, including a Knight. No other Follower or Technology can replace a required Monk. Monks and other substitutions cannot replace the exact professions depicted on Beneficial Deeds, so a Monk cannot substitute for a required Deed profession.
answers.evidence: Monks: a Monk can replace any other profession on ordinary actions; reverse forbidden. Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: substitutions cannot replace exact professions depicted on Deeds.

answers.answer: One Ship moves your Merchant along one Waterway (blue connection) to one adjacent town; one Wagon moves along one Road (brown connection) to one adjacent town. You may collect at most one good from that connection, choosing one if several are there; taking a good is optional. Empty connections are legal and yield no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: Ship uses Waterway, Wagon uses Road; one adjacent town along one connection; collect one good if desired; empty connections legal.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant currently is. A town with any player's station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Building: Guildhall requires Merchant in town; occupied town cannot receive another; Orléans exception.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gives 1 Development Point, moving one space on the Development Track. Moving onto or past a coin space collects its depicted coins; the first player onto or past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching or passing a Development Status space immediately changes your Status to its shown value. The summary does not specify special tie/order handling for simultaneous movement onto reward spaces.
answers.evidence: Actions table: Scriptorium gives 1 Development Point. Scoring / Victory Conditions: rewards on moving onto or past coin, Citizen, and Status spaces.

answers.answer: Town Hall can activate with one or two neutral Followers of any profession, but your four marked starting Followers cannot be used. In one Town Hall action you may send one or both to free Beneficial Deed spaces matching their exact professions, including different Deeds. Each placement gives its depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; at Canalization choose 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The Follower goes permanently onto the Beneficial Deeds board until game end. Whoever fills a Deed's last empty space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: one or two neutral Followers; exact-profession spaces; listed rewards; last space takes Citizen; sent Followers stay.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment in that round's Action Phase; it applies before Phase 5, not at the later event resolution. Other Hour Glass events resolve for all players in Phase 6. The stack is prepared so round 1 always has Pilgrimage, so Pilgrimage opens the game.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Hour Glass and Event; Events: Pilgrimage restricts this round's Action Phase; setup puts Pilgrimage on top.

answers.answer: Harvest food is one grain, cheese, or wine; wool and brocade do not qualify. Pay one qualifying good to the Goods Market. If unable to pay food, pay 5 coins; if unable to pay those coins, undergo torture for the shortfall. The summary does not specify a special Harvest payment destination beyond saying the food is paid to the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Events — Harvest: pay one grain, cheese, or wine to Goods Market; if unable, pay 5 coins; wool and brocade are not food.

answers.answer: If Plague draws a neutral Scholar, return it to its game-board supply, where it becomes recruitable again; do not move its track marker back. If it draws your marked starting Trader, keep it and lose no Follower that round; do not redraw. The summary does not instruct any replacement draw for the starting Trader, and explicitly says not to redraw.
answers.evidence: Events — Plague: neutral returns to supply with no track change; marked starting Follower is kept; lose no Follower; do not redraw.

answers.answer: Pay the one coin you have; each of the two missing coins is replaced with one item, choosing any mix of eligible assets: a built or unbuilt Trading Station, one random eligible Follower from your bag only, one Development Point, one Goods Tile, one Place Tile, or one Technology tile. Market and Action Space Followers are ineligible; if drawing a marked starting Follower, return it and redraw until an eligible neutral one. A Development Point moves one space left but never onto or past a coin space. Surrendered items are removed from the game. The summary says Followers on Action Spaces/Market cannot be used and lists loss of a Development Point; it does not list losing coins as a sacrifice.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy): each missing coin replaced by one item from listed mix; restrictions on Followers and Development Points; items removed from game.

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part of the action would still give a reward. The action becomes available again when its required tile is available, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply is insufficient, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies: cannot play an action providing an unavailable tile, even if another reward; action returns when tile available; insufficient coin supply prevents receipt.

answers.answer: A tie for most built Trading Stations means nobody takes the set-aside bonus Citizen. Each coin scores 1 VP; grain/cheese/wine/wool/brocade score 1/2/3/4/5 VP each. Built Trading Stations plus collected Citizens score (stations + Citizens) × final Development Status. Final-score ties go to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: unique most stations takes Citizen; tie gives nobody; scoring table and tie rules.

answers.answer: Each player takes a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Put the starting Followers on your Market, Merchant in Orléans, and a marker on the first space of each of six Character Tracks and the Development Track. Keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. The youngest player takes the Start Player token. The summary does not say where the seven markers are physically placed beyond specifying their initial track spaces.
answers.evidence: Setup step 2: personal components and placements; youngest takes Start Player token.

answers.answer: In 4 players, put 13 Citizens on their marked board/Beneficial Deeds spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Sort neutral Followers by profession into their game-board buildings, and put Technology and coins in nearby supplies. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II. Shuffle goods face down and deal one face up onto every eligible Road/Waterway goods space; in 4 players fill every such space. Sort remaining goods face up into the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, 5: Citizens, neutral Followers, Technology, Place Tile categories, map goods and Goods Market.

answers.answer: For 3 players remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders each; remove 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks each; remove 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players remove 4 of each Farmer/Boatman/Craftsman/Trader; remove 6 of each Knight/Scholar/Monk; remove 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table and instruction: remove all starting Followers of unused colors.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table, required Followers column.

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table, required Followers column.

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall allows any one or two neutral Followers, of any profession.
answers.evidence: Actions table and Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds section.

answers.answer: Yes. With allowance six, you may decline two draws and instead move one Follower from an Action Space back to your Market for each declined draw. This is the permitted recovery route; you may not move Followers directly from one Action Space to another.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Followers: for each declined draw, move one Follower from Action Space back to Market; cannot move directly between Action Spaces.

answers.answer: Yes. You may inspect your bag at any time, but must shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Followers: may inspect bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.

answers.answer: The seven phases are Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. Pass the Start Player token to the player on your left. Planning begins simultaneously; if order matters, plan clockwise from Start Player. Event payments and any necessary order-sensitive resolution proceed clockwise from Start Player. Coins paid go to the common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phases 1–7; Planning; Event.

answers.answer: You do not score immediately upon revealing the 18th tile. Finish the entire round, including its event, then score.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including its event.

answers.answer: The player uniquely ahead on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin, regardless of how many Farmer tiles players currently have in their bags.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Census: compare Farmers Track markers, regardless of Farmer tiles currently in bags; unique leader gains 1 coin.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Events — Income: gain coins equal to Development Status.

answers.answer: With eight goods, pay 2 coins (one per complete group of three, rounding down). Goods types do not change the count. If short, torture applies for the shortfall; the summary does not state a different Taxes-specific payment rule.
answers.evidence: Events — Taxes: count all goods; pay 1 coin per complete group of 3, round down; shortfall causes torture.

answers.answer: Receive 4 coins, one per built Trading Station. The six unbuilt stations in reserve do not count.
answers.evidence: Events — Trading Day: gain 1 coin per built Trading Station; Building says only built stations count for income.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer; take 1 grain from the Goods Market. Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer; take 1 cheese from the Goods Market. Winery: Farmer + Trader; take 1 wine from the Goods Market. Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader; take 1 wool from the Goods Market. Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader; take 1 brocade from the Goods Market. A goods-producing Place cannot be used when that particular good is absent from the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table; following sentence: goods-producing Place cannot be used when its good is absent.

answers.answer: Shipping Line requires Boatman and gives 1 Development Point. Brewery requires Monk and gives 2 coins. Windmill requires Craftsman + Craftsman and gives 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library requires Knight + Scholar and gives 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Pharmacy can be activated by any 1 Follower. You must pay 1–3 coins, advancing one Development space per coin paid. Paying two advances two spaces. Zero and four coins are not legal: minimum is one, maximum is three.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table: Any 1 Follower; pay 1–3; one Development space per coin; must spend at least 1 and no more than 3.

answers.answer: Cellar requires Monk + Scholar and gives 4 coins. Office requires Scholar + Scholar and gives 1 coin per Trading Station you have built. Hospital requires Boatman + Scholar and gives coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight. It moves along one Road to an adjacent town and collects one good if available.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile, subject to usual placement constraints. Your first Technology cannot be placed on Laboratory, because it must replace a Farmer and Laboratory has no Farmer space. A later Technology may be placed on either Laboratory space if none is already there and usual constraints are met.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table — Laboratory; technology placement constraints.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately place the chosen tiles on appropriate Action Spaces; none may go on Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag. The summary does not specify an additional timing condition for when during the round the chosen tiles are placed.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table — Bathhouse.

answers.answer: You may place the one Follower that can legally fit on an allowed Action Space. Return the other drawn Followers and the activating Farmer to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Farmer to your bag.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table — Bathhouse: if only one or none can be legally placed, do so and return all other drawn Followers; return activating Follower.

answers.answer: It may be executed later in the same Action Phase on one of your later action turns, provided you have not passed. A Place completed during the Action Phase is available on a later action turn in that phase.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Actions: a Place completed during this phase is available on a later one of your action turns in the same phase; passing is final.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 you may return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague. The Monk goes back to your bag.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table — Sacristy.

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5 (Actions). Sacristy's protection is used in Phase 6, so it does not permit recruiting a Monk earlier in the round.
answers.evidence: Events — Pilgrimage applies to Action Phase; Sacristy protection occurs during Phase 6.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not allow replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table — Herb Garden.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It requires no activation. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table — School.

answers.answer: No. Herb Garden and School substitution abilities apply to ordinary actions; Beneficial Deed spaces require exact professions and substitutions cannot replace them. Using Gunpowder Tower instead of Town Hall does not change this: Deed spaces still require exact types.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: substitutions cannot replace exact professions; Herb Garden/School specify ordinary actions; Gunpowder Tower retains exact Deed types.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3, place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. In Planning, move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, in one action send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds. You cannot send marked starting Followers, and Deed spaces require exact professions. The summary does not give any other destination for Followers placed in the Tower.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles table — Gunpowder Tower.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two tied furthest behind pay nothing because a tied last place pays nothing.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Census: unique leader gains 1 coin; tied last place pays nothing.

answers.answer: The uniquely leading player in built Trading Stations takes the set-aside Citizen after the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn is finished, including its event, before scoring. It counts as a collected Citizen in final station/Citizen scoring. The summary says the pre-scoring unique leader takes the Citizen and collected Citizens are included in the formula.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: finish round 18 including event; before scoring unique most built stations takes set-aside Citizen; scoring formula includes collected Citizens.

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage Hour Glass tile, shuffle the other 17 face down, then put the removed Pilgrimage on top. In Phase 1 the Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup: remove lighter Pilgrimage, shuffle other 17, put Pilgrimage on top. Turn Structure — Hour Glass: Start Player reveals top tile.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions table: Coins — 1 each.

answers.answer: Initial Development Status is 1, and initial Knight-track draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup step 2: Development Status starts at 1; initial draw allowance is 4.

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Goods, Followers, Trading Stations, Places, and Technology surrendered to torture are removed from the game rather than returned to their supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture: surrendered items removed from game; only lost Development Points can be regained.

answers.answer: You may choose the order freely; you need not follow printed board order or the order in which actions were filled.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Actions: choose your actions' order freely.

answers.answer: Its passive substitution ability is available immediately, including during the current Action Phase; you do not wait until the next round.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment — Trader: acquired Place and passive special ability available immediately, including current Action Phase.

answers.answer: You may send just one; a Town Hall action sends one or both eligible Followers to matching free Deed spaces.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: in one Town Hall action, send one or both.

answers.answer: Taking a good is optional; you may complete the move and leave the available good on the connection.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: taking a good during Ship or Wagon is optional; may leave available good.

answers.answer: Yes. You may send the two Town Hall Followers in separate action turns during the same Action Phase, before you pass. The second transfer need not occur in the same Town Hall action.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: may send two Followers in separate action turns during same Action Phase before passing.
